figures.caption: Figure 1. Our computational simulation workflow for SSB composite cathodes. The process begins with the wet manufacturing simulation (from slurry to calendered electrode), followed by a half-cell mechano-electrochemical assessment based on coupled equations of electrochemistry, mass transport, and mechanics. The two physics (electrochemistry and mechanics) are fully coupled: lithium concentration–dependent volume changes influence the electrochemical response, while the mechanical feedback to electrochemistry is introduced via a stress-dependent mechano-chemical potential. This bidirectional interaction between electrochemical properties and mechanical behavior forms a closed feedback loop that is resolved through the tracking of microstructure evolution.
